body:
I understand why you are concerned about the performance, but your number 1 problem to solve is this:

```
# Out of bounds values : 64 FAILED
```

This is *not* supposed to happen. You've got some data corruption going on, possibly hardware-related. Given that disabling ECE in IB gives you your performance back, I would suspect the NICs first. You can try to limit the set of RDMA interfaces used by NCCL by setting `NCCL_IB_HCA`. Are low-level IB/RDMA tests passing (see https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting.html#networking-issues)?
Those tests are showing *massive* data corruption `4.09366e+09`

We also noted data corruption in the nccl-test here.

I will rephrase this issue to make it easier for us to understand.
Firstly, I ran NCCL tests using NCCL-2.19.3 in the `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.12-py3` and `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.06-py3` containers. We found that the performance data in the `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.12-py3` container was as expected, but the performance data in the `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.06-py3` container was significantly below the expected values. The log files are in `result_23.12.txt` and `result_24.06.txt`, respectively. 

[result_23.12.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16620551/result_23.12.txt)
[result_24.06.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16620553/result_24.06.txt)

Our analysis of the logs revealed that the only difference between the two was the version of IBext used—one was IBext_v6, and the other was IBext_v7. After replacing the `/opt/hpcx/nccl_rdma_sharp_plugin/lib/libnccl-net.so` file in the nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.06-py3 container with the corresponding file from the nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.12-py3 container, we found that the performance in the nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.06-py3 container was also as expected and correct.

Our further analysis suggests that the difference between the two libnccl-net.so files might be related to whether the ECE feature is enabled. We replicated this issue using the NCCL-2.22.3 version, as discussed above. However, after using NCCL-2.22.3, there were many data errors.

Let’s return to the core issue: using NCCL-2.19.3, but with different libnccl-net.so files, results in significant performance differences. Could you provide some assistance with this issue @AddyLaddy @kiskra-nvidia ?

 (We will also further explore the data corruption in NCCL tests later.)

### Issue Cleanup: Helping Us Focus on Current Challenges

We're [reviewing](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/discussions/1761) older issues to ensure we prioritize the most relevant and active ones. Since this issue hasn't seen updates in over 6 months, we'll be closing it for now.
